Why Bearman is yet to be announced as a Haas driver for F1 2027

DM
By David Miller Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist • via Autosport Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Autosport Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year.
  • There is no real doubt that Bearman will stay where he is, with both parties keen to continue for another season into 2027.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • DAVID MILLER Formula 1 & Motorsport Telemetry Specialist

Aerodynamic Efficiency & Motorsport Racecraft

In premier motorsport disciplines, millisecond gains represent months of high-intensity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) research. The developments reported by Autosport underline how tire degradation curves, ground-effect aero seals, and power-unit energy recovery systems dictate race outcomes. Technical compliance under strict cost caps continues to test team engineering depth.

Big Picture: Upcoming grand prix telemetry and trackside upgrades will reveal which teams hold the definitive technical advantage.

With Oliver Bearman firing on all cylinders in his sophomore Formula 1 campaign, it feels odd that Haas has been able to confirm the identity of Esteban Ocon's replacement in the second seat for 2027 before announcing Bearman is staying put for a third year.

📌 The Core Development

There is no real doubt that Bearman will stay where he is, with both parties keen to continue for another season into 2027.

“I think it's very clear. I want to continue with Haas and that's definitely my goal," Bearman said in Mexico on Thursday. "It's not really in my hands. If it was up to me, it would have already been announced a long time ago, but there are a few bigger picture things that we're working on."

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Team principal Komatsu added: "I don't like to go into the details of our contract, but Ollie is showing amazing potential. He's contributing a lot to the team's success and we want to grow together. We want to move up the grid as a team.”

And while Komatsu had to dismiss unsubstantiated rumours over Bearman's pay demands, holding up a deal as "absolute nonsense", the real reason behind the delay is not about 2027, but about what happens next.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Autosport understands that should Ferrari be unable to guarantee him a seat in 2028 - after three years of being loaned out to customer team Haas - then Bearman will have the freedom to part ways with Maranello. It is this "bigger picture" that Bearman was referring to in his answer, and a picture that has become increasingly clouded in recent months.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Bearman is still on course to complete the full Ferrari Driver Academy pathway, all the way from F4 to a race seat with the Scuderia - Charles Leclerc being the only driver thus far to have completed the entire trajectory.

But a new road block has emerged in the shape of Lewis Hamilton, who has regained form this year and exercised the contractual option that secured his place at Ferrari for 2027. While Bearman initially looked like a perfect successor to Hamilton, the seven-time world champion's recent comments in the media about his longevity do not portray a man who is walking away from Ferrari and F1 anytime soon. Leclerc, meanwhile, has already agreed a long-term contract extension until at least 2030.
